To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

zenk mRNA expression was found in all auditory brain areas, including those associated with vocal learning, and that the distribution of zenk mRNA expression is similar to that of zenk protein expression in the budgerigar.

contact calls drive zenk mRNA expression, that the pattern of zenk mRNA expression induced by contact calls is highly similar to the distribution of zenk protein expression induced by contact call stimulation, and that zenk protein and zenk mRNA expression are not mutually exclusive.

zenk (zift68, egr1) mRNA is expressed in the brain in response to contact calls in a vocal learning bird, the budgeriagar (Melopsittacius undulatus), and that the distribution of zenk mRNA expression is consistent with the distribution of zen protein and with the known distribution of neurons in the vocal system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the neuroanatomy and neurochemistry of brain areas associated with the vocal learning system of budgerigars, a parrot species with a vocal repertoire that is similar in many respects to that of songbirds.
the molecular mechanisms of vocal learning in birds.
the neural mechanisms that underlie the development of the ability to learn and use complex vocalizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zenk gene is expressed in the vocal system in the budgerigar, but that there is a difference between the zenk protein and zenk mRNA distribution.
zenk is expressed in all auditory and vocal motor areas of the budgerigars brain.
the zenk gene is expressed throughout the entire vocal system in budgerigar brain, and that zenk mRNA expression is induced by contact call stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
zenk expression in the vocal system is contact-call driven and zenk protein is localized in perikaryal and/or dendritic regions of neurons.
zenk expression is a general indicator of neural activation and is not limited to specific cell populations.

zenk protein and zenk mRNA expression patterns are highly congruent in budgerigarrs and zenk protein and gene expression are both highly congruent with the distribution of neurons exhibiting song-related gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contact call-stimulation induces zenk mRNA expression across a broad area of the brain.
the zenk mRNA distribution is similar to the distribution of zenk protein.
zenk expression is induced by auditory stimulation in the vocal system of the budgerigars, a vocal learning species.
